newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Opponents press for talks with Kabila.
newsitem.headline: Opponents press for talks with Kabila.

text.p: A Congolese opposition leader on Saturday called for a round-table meeting with President Laurent Kabila to discuss power-sharing and said the opposition might resort to violence if the talks did not get off the ground.

Roger Lumbala, leader of the Rally for the Congolese People (RPC), told Reuters in an interview that the meeting should gather together the "main political forces" in the renamed Democratic Republic of the Congo.

"There are two ways of conducting a struggle. The thing is to choose between the political and the armed struggle. If they oppose the round-table meeting, we will feel free to resort to violence to put our ideas forward," Lumbala said.
"We've set no deadline yet for the talks. We want to negotiate. But if President Kabila's door is still closed, he will bear the consequences," he said.
Lumbala's RPC is mainly led by former exiles who returned home after Kabila ousted former dictator Mobutu Sese Seko.
President Kabila's cabinet is dominated by members of his Alliance of the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of the Congo.
However, local newspapers have said that a thorough cabinet reshuffle is in the offing, and the new government could include representatives of the major political groups.

La Reference daily has said that veteran opposition politicain Etienne Tshisekedi could be given the post of premier. He claims that he should already be prime minister, based on decisions taken by a 1992 national conference.
